source.title: Gaussian Perturbations in ReLU Networks and the Arrangement of Activation Regions

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper titled “Tangent Space Sensitivity and Distribution of Linear Regions in ReLU Networks,” which does not match the provided title “Gaussian Perturbations in ReLU Networks and the Arrangement of Activation Regions.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures whether tangent-sensitivity estimates track empirical test loss and accuracy on CIFAR-10. This bears on the broad claim that trained-network properties relate to the generalization gap, but it does not test the specific properties or interventions in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The reported MAEs compare three tangent-sensitivity estimates of test cross-entropy loss and accuracy. Cited findings about other measures and methods are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates tangent-sensitivity bounds and test-performance estimators, which measure a different construct from V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness. It reports no results testing V1–V8. Listing SGD, Adam and dropout variants does not establish comparative generalization effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors connect tangent sensitivity to active paths, weight norms and activation-region distributions, and present preliminary CIFAR-10 evidence that their estimators approximate changes in empirical generalization gap. They call for further investigation and extension beyond fully connected ReLU networks and smooth input transformations.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates tangent-sensitivity-based estimates of test loss and accuracy; it does not apply the interventions or measures in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported estimation errors differ by estimator and metric: empirical sensitivity has the lowest cross-entropy MAE, while layer-wise log-norm sensitivity has the lowest accuracy MAE.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports test cross-entropy estimation MAEs of 0.00053, 0.00077 and 0.00042, and accuracy estimation MAEs of 0.0092, 0.0098 and 0.011, for the three tangent-sensitivity estimators.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tangent-sensitivity estimators can approximate held-out loss and accuracy across training states of fully connected ReLU networks on CIFAR-10.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says it plans to share the Python source code.
record.problems: The experiments use fully connected ReLU networks on CIFAR-10. The reported metric is estimation MAE rather than a direct test of the train–test generalization gap; uncertainty estimates are not stated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; Figure 2 varies a sensitivity bound, not measured test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error; dropout variants are listed without comparative outcomes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, including rankings against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text identifies itself as arXiv:2006.06780, Tangent Space Sensitivity and Distribution of Linear Regions in ReLU Networks. Its correspondence to the supplied DOI is unresolved; this verdict applies to the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.
